pre-commit.description: Ships disabled; enabledManagers alone does not turn it on.

major.description: Majors wait for a human on the dependency dashboard.

packageRules.description: One pull request per run for the ordinary updates. Each merge that touches a deploy path costs a pipeline execution and an MFA approval, and a CodePipeline stage lock means a second merge cannot be drained until the first is approved and applied — so the cost of review is per-PR, not per-dependency. Majors are excluded and stay individually reviewable.

Pre-1.0 minors can break, and Renovate still classes them minor, so the major gate above misses them. Ungrouped deliberately: bundled into the batch, one 0.x dependency would hold the whole group behind an approval. Not enabled:false — that is evaluated before updateType exists, so pairing it with matchUpdateTypes silently never matches.

renovatebot/pre-commit-hooks publishes several releases a day, so something has always just cleared the seven-day soak and there is permanently an open pull request for it — merging faster never catches up. The hook only validates a Renovate config file, so nothing downstream needs it current to the hour; it batches monthly instead. Ungrouped so the schedule applies to it rather than to whatever else shares its group.
